data.title: SAP Says No Decisions Made on Job Cuts as AI Reshapes Landscape
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

SAP said it is continuously reviewing how its organization and workforce need to evolve as artificial intelligence rapidly reshapes the business environment, but that no decisions have been made on restructuring or job cuts.

A spokesperson for the German business-software group made the comments after Bloomberg reported, citing unnamed sources, that the company was exploring at least 10,000 job cuts in response to the accelerating AI shift.

Bloomberg reported that discussions were continuing, and that the restructuring could affect at least 9% of the group's global workforce, although the total number of jobs hadn't yet been finalized.

The SAP spokesperson said job roles and functions would naturally change over time, but beyond that, no decisions had been made regarding any further measures.

"We do not comment on speculation," the spokesperson said.

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com

data.title: EQT to Buy Majority Stake in Specialty European Pharmaceutical Group Kelso Pharma
data.description:
(07:03 GMT) *EQT to Buy Majority Stake in Specialty European Pharmaceutical Business Kelso Pharma
(07:04 GMT) *EQT Agrees to Buy Majority Stake in Kelso Pharma From Healthcare Investment Firm Apposite Capital
(07:05 GMT) *EQT: Kelso Pharma Has Portfolio of Medicines Mainly for Endocrine, Gastrointestinal, Central Nervous System Conditions
(07:35 GMT) EQT to Buy Majority Stake in Specialty European Pharmaceutical Group Kelso Pharma

By Dominic Chopping

Swedish buyout group EQT said it agreed to acquire a majority stake in specialty pharmaceutical group Kelso Pharma from healthcare-investment firm Apposite Capital.

Founded in 2021, Kelso Pharma is a European group with a portfolio of around 14 medicines, mainly for endocrine, gastrointestinal and central nervous system conditions. They are sold through its own U.K.-based commercial infrastructure and exported to more than 30 countries globally.

Kelso Pharma is working to expand the product range to provide additional medicines. EQT said it would support the pharmaceutical company's expansion across Europe through investment in its commercial capabilities, new product launches and selective acquisitions and licensing agreements.

Kelso's management team, led by Chief Executive Officer Tom Stratford, will continue to lead the company.

"Healthcare systems across Europe are increasingly looking to specialist companies to serve patient groups that larger pharmaceutical businesses often overlook," said Mark Braganza, partner at EQT Healthcare Growth.

"With an experienced team, its own commercial infrastructure and a portfolio serving niche patient populations, Kelso has built a strong U.K.-based business with the foundations to grow as a pan-European platform."

The deal is expected to close during the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary conditions and approvals.

data.title: Vanke proposes extending 95% of bond repayment due December 15 by 3 years, sources say
data.description:
Embattled property developer China Vanke has proposed to repay 5% of its onshore bond principal due on December 15, while extending the remainder by three years, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Friday.

The people declined to be identified because the proposed details are not public yet.

This would be the second extension of the bond in question that matures on December 15 (CN102282715=) - with an outstanding 1.2 billion yuan ($180.33 million) - highlighting that the financial stress is far from over for one of China's best-known real estate developers.

Vanke has extended 60% of the repayments by a year for its onshore bonds that came due during the past 12 months.

With more than $50 billion in debt, Vanke is among the last major distressed firms trying to avert a default in the country's protracted property crisis, during which many of its rivals, big and small, have defaulted on their debt repayments.

A default by Vanke, which has many projects in top-tier cities, could further dampen already weak homebuyer confidence and weigh on the broader economy, which is grappling with sluggish growth and tepid consumer spending.

In the latest proposal, the company also suggested it could defer interest payments during the extension period until the new maturity date of December 15, 2029.

Vanke did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The company will hold a bondholder meeting to vote on the extension plan on December 8.

($1 = 6.6543 yuan)

data.title: Wall St futures surge as investors return from holiday
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 0.89%, S&P 500 1.65%, Nasdaq 2.47%

US stock futures surged on Friday, led by contracts tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 index, as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday with renewed appetite for beaten-down shares.

Wall Street's main indexes have swung sharply this week after Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO and Anthropic's slide below its IPO price.

AI stocks have seesawed as investors weigh more attractive valuations against persistent concerns about heavy spending on the technology.

"The recovery in stocks seems technical. The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB.

"If these gains can be sustained on Friday, it would suggest that enthusiasm for the AI trade is back."

At 2:13 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) jumped 446 points, or 0.89%, S&P 500 E-minis rose 119 points, or 1.65%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis surged 645.75 points, or 2.47%.

A hawkish Federal Reserve, however, remains one of the top risks for stocks. Data this week showed the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation accelerated further in October, reinforcing expectations of a rate hike.

Traders are pricing in a 99% chance of a rate hike next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Wall Street was closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

data.title: Japan futures post weekly gain as oil stays firm
data.description:
By Emily Ou Yong

Japanese rubber futures were steady and logged a weekly gain on Friday, supported by oil prices hovering near this month's high, although soft tyre demand limited gains.

  • The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for May delivery , was little changed at 430.6 yen ($2.70) per kg

  • The contract gained 1.72% this week

  • The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery rose 300 yuan, or 1.62%, to 18,830 yuan ($2,829.75) per metric ton

  • The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 100 yuan, or 0.65%, to 15,380 yuan per metric ton

  • Oil prices rose slightly on Friday and are on track to snap a three-week losing streak as ongoing attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil supply from the conflict-hit Middle East

  • Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil

  • Tyre makers may be digesting channel inventory without raising output, which suggests end-user demand is weaker than expected, analysts from broker Zijin Tianfeng Futures said in a note

  • The operating rate of China's all-steel tyre makers fell 2.38 percentage points to 53.83% in the week ended November 26, from 56.21% a week earlier, data from rubber information provider Qinrex showed

  • Affordability is likely to remain the principal constraint on mass-market vehicle demand in 2027, following modest growth in 2026, said Fitch Ratings in a report

  • Automobile sales could influence the intensity of automobile manufacturing, which involves using rubber-made tyres

  • The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 240.2 US cents per kg, up 1.4% as of 0700 GMT

($1 = 159.2500 yen)

data.title: OEM International appoints Henrik Forsberg Schoultz as President and CEO
data.description:
The Board of OEM International AB (“OEM”) has appointed Henrik Forsberg Schoultz as President and CEO, effective 1 January 2027. He succeeds Jörgen Zahlin, who has served as CEO of OEM International for 27 years and has been with the Group for a total of 41 years, and will remain as senior advisor during 2027.

Henrik has been Deputy CEO of OEM since April 2026, responsible for group strategy, the acquisition agenda and the development of the business portfolio. He has extensive experience of long-term value creation in acquisition-driven companies, with a strong focus on entrepreneur-led companies in decentralised environments. Prior to OEM, he was President and CEO of CellMark AB, has held senior leadership and investment roles at Neudi & Co and Nordstjernan, and started his career at McKinsey & Company.

Patrik Andersson, Chairman, says: “I am pleased to appoint Henrik as CEO. During his time at OEM he has gained a thorough understanding of the business, its unique culture and what it takes to position the company for the future. He has the leadership and experience needed to guide OEM through its next phase of growth. On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank Jörgen Zahlin for his contributions over more than four decades in making OEM the company it is today.”

“It is a great honour to be entrusted with leading OEM. Jörgen and our employees have built a strong platform, with a close focus on customers and suppliers and a unique culture with its home in Tranås. We will preserve and build on that position, while further accelerating capital deployment and continuing to grow profitably across Europe.” says Henrik Forsberg Schoultz

Jörgen Zahlin comments: “It has been a privilege to lead OEM and to work alongside so many dedicated colleagues and partners. I am proud of what we have achieved together and of the strong position OEM holds today. I wish Henrik every success in his new role and look forward to supporting him going forward.”

This information is information that OEM International is obliged to make public pursuant to the EU Market Abuse Regulation. The information was submitted for publication, through the agency of the contact persons set out below, at 2026-11-27 08:30 CET.

Contacts

For further information, please contact Patrik Andersson, Chairman of the Board, OEM International AB, on +46 76-111 34 00, or Daniel Warnholtz, CFO, OEM International AB, on +46 75-242 40 18 or via email at daniel.warnholtz@oem.se.

About Us

OEM International is one of Europe's leading technology trading companies with 39 operating units in 16 countries. The group operates in the trade of components and systems from leading suppliers in selected markets in Europe. A well-structured local market organisation and efficient logistics make OEM a better alternative to the supplier’s own sales organisations.

For more information see www.oem.se

data.title: Ladbrokes Owner Entain Reaches $123 Million Pact to Settle Australia Probe
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Ladbrokes owner Entain said it reached a preliminary agreement with Australian authorities to pay 185 million Australian dollars ($122.7 million) to settle an antimoney-laundering and counterterrorist financing probe that led to a lawsuit.

The U.K. gambling group said Friday that its deal with the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre seeks to resolve civil penalty proceedings brought against the company over Entain Australia's contraventions of the Australian Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 between December 2018 and August 2024.

The company said a proposed statement of agreed facts and admissions and the civil penalty remain subject to approval by its board of directors, Austrac and the Federal Court of Australia. Subject to the timing of final approvals, the company expects to fully pay the fine by the end of the year.

Entain said it cooperated with Austrac throughout its investigation and put in place significant enhancements to the antimoney-laundering and counterterrorist-financing systems, processes and controls of its Australian business.

"This is an important step towards resolving a legacy issue for the group and our local business," Entain Chief Executive Stella David said.

Write to Adria Calatayud at adria.calatayud@wsj.com

data.title: Isofol has received a top guarantee commitment for the exercise of warrants of series TO2
data.description:
GOTHENBURG, Sweden, November 27, 2026 – Isofol Medical AB ("Isofol" or the "Company") announces that the Company has received a top guarantee commitment totalling SEK 16.5 million, corresponding to approximately 44 per cent of the proceeds from the full exercise of the warrants of series TO2. The Company carried out a rights issue of units in June/July 2025. In connection with the rights issue, Isofol issued a total of 39,863,928 warrants of series TO2. The exercise period for the warrants of series TO2 runs from 16 November 2026 up to and including 30 November 2026. Together with the subscription commitments from major shareholders, Board members and management of approximately SEK 5.8 million announced on 24 November 2026, and Solasia Pharma K.K.'s stated intention to exercise all of its warrants of series TO2 of approximately SEK 2.0 million, the exercise of the warrants of series TO2 is thereby covered by subscription commitments, a statement of intent and a top guarantee totalling approximately SEK 24.3 million, corresponding to approximately 64 per cent of the proceeds upon full exercise of the warrants of series TO2.

The information in this press release is intended for investors.

For further information, please see the section “Important information” at the end of this press release.

Top guarantee commitment

The Company has entered into a top guarantee agreement with ABG Sundal Collier ASA (the "Guarantor"). Under the top guarantee, the Guarantor has undertaken to guarantee SEK 16.5 million, corresponding to approximately 44 per cent of the proceeds that the Company may receive upon full exercise of the warrants of series TO2. The top guarantee will lapse if the warrants of series TO2 are exercised in full. If the top guarantee is called upon, in whole or in part, the Guarantor will subscribe for shares in a directed share issue in the Company at a subscription price corresponding to the fixed exercise price of the warrants of series TO2, SEK 0.95 per share.

If the Guarantor's top guarantee is called upon, Isofol's Board of Directors intends to exercise the authorisation granted by the Annual General Meeting on 19 May 2026 and resolve on a directed share issue on the same terms as those applicable to the exercise of TO2. The top guarantee commitment has been provided in return for a cash fee of nine (9) per cent of the guaranteed amount. The guarantee commitment has been agreed in writing but has not been secured by a bank guarantee, blocked funds, a pledge or similar arrangements, and there is therefore a risk that the guarantee commitment will not be fulfilled.

About Isofol

Isofol Medical AB (publ) is a clinical stage biotechnology company focused on improving outcomes for patients with severe forms of cancer. Arfolitixorin is currently being evaluated in phase Ib/II in colorectal cancer, the world’s third most common cancer, where there is a significant unmet medical need.
